summary: Compare how Kafka, RabbitMQ and Redis Streams publish orders, track progress and recover unfinished work.
scope: Three lanes use the same illustrative order workflow: a Kafka partition, a RabbitMQ work queue, and a Redis Stream with a consumer group.
author: Thoth

sources.title: Apache Kafka · Event streaming and partitions

componentNotes.client: The online store is the producer. When a customer places an order, the store sends Kafka a message with the order number so other parts of the system can react.
componentNotes.publisher: The online store is the producer. It sends RabbitMQ a job to prepare the order for shipping. A worker picks up the job and does the work.
componentNotes.redis-producer: The online store is the producer. It adds a new order to the Redis stream with the XADD command so a worker can pick it up.
componentNotes.log: Records receive offsets within this partition and remain readable according to retention settings.
componentNotes.consumers: Independent consumer groups can read the same partition at different paces. Each group commits its own offsets.
componentNotes.exchange: Routes messages to queues according to exchange type and bindings. Multiple matching queues can receive copies.
componentNotes.queue: Holds work until delivery and tracks unacknowledged deliveries. A delivered message can return to the queue if its consumer disconnects.
componentNotes.worker: Acknowledges a delivery after processing succeeds.
componentNotes.stream: XADD appends an entry with a stream ID. An acknowledgement clears the pending entry for that group. Retention is managed separately.
componentNotes.redis-worker: XREADGROUP assigns entries to a consumer and tracks them as pending. A worker acknowledges completed entries with XACK or claims idle pending entries with XAUTOCLAIM.
